solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Around middle of board puts kings and queens here?

indicators.note: the pick from the board sits with a word wrapped around it, so the outer word encloses it

parts.note: to put something is to place it, so puts means places

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word board is taken

explanation.surface: A chess observation about what happens when pieces reach the centre of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts A, the middle letter of boArd, inside PLACES. The chessboard's kings and queens are a red herring: the definition means real royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal residences are where monarchs live, hence the question mark on this playful definition by example.

clue.text: Well-mannered coppers with time for first of complaints

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: coppers is slang for police officers

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word complaints is taken

explanation.surface: Polite officers dealing with complaints in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps C, the first letter of complaints, out of POLICE and puts T in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being courteous and having good manners are synonyms.

clue.text: Where Boris Johnson might be eccentric, embracing leaders in New Delhi

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other letters in its arms, so they go inside

parts.note: a loon is an eccentric, crazy person

indicators.note: the leading letters of the two words New and Delhi are taken

explanation.surface: A jibe that the former mayor might be odd and hugging Indian bigwigs in Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was Mayor of London when this appeared, so the city is where he might be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson was mayor of the British capital at the time, so the capital is where one would find him.

clue.text: Letters from prisoners upsetting to nans

parts.note: cons is short for convicts, prisoners

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters of to nans are scrambled

explanation.surface: Grandmothers distressed by letters from inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests mail from prison; it means alphabet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters other than vowels such as B, C and D form one class of the alphabet's letters.

clue.text: Talk about Western type of jazz

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talk goes round the letter

parts.note: to sing is slang for talking, informing to police

explanation.surface: A discussion about a jazz style from the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Big-band dance music of the 1930s and 40s is a jazz style, so the definition names its genre.

clue.text: Flower's dropping, overrun by returning crowd

indicators.note: the drop is swamped by the crowd's letters on both sides, so it sits inside them
the word for a crowd is read backwards, coming back the other way

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
a loss is a dropping or falling away, as in a drop in value

explanation.surface: A flower is wilting while being trampled by a crowd heading back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the crowd word and 'overrun by' puts the drop inside it. 'Flower' is the bloom, not something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloom on a fruit tree is a flower, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Excellent fish ain't at sea!

parts.note: brill is a flatfish related to turbot

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the word are mixed up

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the fish is excellent because it isn't in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives of high praise meaning outstanding.

clue.text: Casanova love-nest taking shape

indicators.note: the run of letters is taken from within the words Casanova love-nest

explanation.surface: Casanova's love-nest is starting to take form.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-like outline is a geometric shape, so the definition is its general class.

clue.text: Footwear for those who fall over?

definitions.meaning: soft indoor shoes worn at home
people who slip and tumble, read playfully as slip-ers

explanation.definitionFit: Indoor shoes are footwear, and the word read playfully also means people who slide and tumble.

clue.text: About ready?

parts.note: about means concerning and ready is slang for cash, so concerning cash

explanation.definitionFit: Ready is British slang for money, so something concerning cash relates to money in a financial sense.

clue.text: Crease knight's cloth

parts.note: a crease is a line in fabric or skin
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight's garment has a crease in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric woven from flax is a familiar cloth, so the definition names it by its general class.

clue.text: Fake qualification left out

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: a qualification is a limitation or restriction placed on a statement

explanation.surface: A forged certificate whose holder was left off the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Qualification' suggests a diploma, which fits 'Fake'; here it means a restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something counterfeit or a copy is a fake, used as a noun in both cases.

clue.text: Really hot nuts, say

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, telling us to jumble the letters of the word hot

parts.note: say used as approximately, as in say ten, means roughly

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the nuts are really hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the snack being described; it is the anagram signal turning HOT into THO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs of degree meaning completely or utterly, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Small hole for capturing animals — this might be released from the trap

definitions.text: this might be released from the trap

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pit dug and covered is a trap for animals

explanation.surface: Instructions on digging a little pit to catch animals, with a remark about what escapes the trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is British slang for the mouth, so what is released from it is saliva; the animal trap of the surface is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saliva expelled from the mouth is spittle, which leaves through the mouth, slangily the trap.

clue.text: Feeling blue?

definitions.meaning: the mood or ambience of a place
the blue sky is the air surrounding the earth

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a place's mood and the envelope of air that looks blue as sky.

clue.text: Fellow switched future car brand

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: switched means swapped around, so the letters of future car are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has changed the make of the car he will buy.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a company's name for its products, so a carmaker is loosely a brand.

clue.text: Any Lulu moves captivating American, surprisingly

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the abbreviation goes inside
moves means the letters of Any Lulu shift around

explanation.surface: Any dance moves by the singer Lulu enchant an American, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges ANY LULU and 'captivating' puts US inside. Lulu is a Scottish pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe something out of the ordinary, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Country clubs? Lad's not excited about that

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the card suit letter
excited means stirred up, so the letters of Lad's not are mixed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A lad shows no enthusiasm for a nation's golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges LADSNOT and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern nation of the UK is a country, so the definition names its class.

clue.text: Criticism in article lay badly with sibling

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: badly means the letters of lay are put in a poor order

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: A critical piece in a newspaper was badly set out with help from a sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical examination of a work is criticism in the sense of literary analysis, a synonym.

clue.text: Engineer cut iron cost with new building

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to an engineer to save money on iron in a new building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a person; it is a verb, the anagram signal for CUT IRON COST plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of building something, or the thing built, is a synonym of construction.

clue.text: 10 American soldiers lifted seal

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means raised up, read bottom to top

parts.note: the number ten written as a word
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Ten US troops raised a seal.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is the number, not a reference to 10-across. 'lifted' reverses the whole of TENGIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a stamp of authority, and the ring bearing such an engraved stamp is a synonym.

clue.text: Failing to follow advertisement's counsel

indicators.note: to follow means coming after, so the word for failing comes after the abbreviation

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement
a vice is a failing or moral weakness

explanation.surface: A failure to follow an advert's suggestions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like a verb; it is a noun meaning a weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel and guidance are synonyms when meaning recommendation given to someone.

clue.text: Farm register

definitions.meaning: to farm the land is to cultivate or plough it, a verb sense
a cash register in a shop is the drawer for money

explanation.definitionFit: One word is a verb for working soil and also the shop's cash drawer, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: In new fashion, dump tie? Ill bred

indicators.note: a new fashion rearranges things, telling us to reorder these letters

explanation.surface: A remark that throwing away a tie is in fashion, followed by a scornful 'ill bred'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill bred' looks like a phrase; 'Ill' is fodder and 'bred' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that breed increase in number, so bred is a synonym of increased in number.

clue.text: Catches bugs around river

indicators.note: around means the word for bugs goes round the river's letter

parts.note: to bug a phone is to tap it, so bugs means taps

explanation.surface: Someone catches insects near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bugs' reads as insects; here it means listening devices, so taps.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices that catch animals are snares, so catches as a noun matches by synonym.

clue.text: Type of exam — enters for a laugh

indicators.note: enters means the answer sits inside the words for a laugh

explanation.surface: Someone enters an examination just for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as opposed to a written one, is a type of exam.

clue.text: Almost everyone is in one country or another

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the country's name

parts.note: Austria is the country named here

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A comment that nearly everybody lives in one nation or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter and 'in' places the result inside the country. 'one country' gives the wordplay, so 'or another' alone is the definition: a different nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition means a second nation besides the first named, and the answer is such a nation.

clue.text: In French, starts to nag us, implying boredom

parts.note: en is the French word for in

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone says the French begin nagging us, which shows they are bored.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless weariness from lack of interest is boredom, the borrowed French word being its synonym.

clue.text: Daughter is to perform in show

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
to play is to perform, as on stage or an instrument

explanation.surface: A daughter has a part to perform in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to exhibit or put it on view, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Reset PC to correct after‑image?

indicators.note: correcting means putting the letters right by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Restarting a computer to fix a ghost image on the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a computer glitch; 'Reset PC' is fodder and 'to correct' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostly image left on the eye or a display is a phantom, a sense of the word for an apparition.
